name: Apollos
overview: Apollos was a Jewish believer from Alexandria, described as an eloquent and knowledgeable teacher of the Scriptures who fervently taught about the Lord, though initially he only knew the baptism of John (Acts 18:24-25). After receiving further instruction in the way of God from Aquila and Priscilla, he boldly proclaimed Jesus as the Christ, effectively convincing many Jews publicly (Acts 18:26-28). His ministry was impactful in Corinth, where he helped many believers grow in grace, and he was commended by the early church for his teaching and encouragement (Acts 18:27; 19:1).
